title: Employee wage records for labour inspection audits

F-R1.quote: To verify that employers inspected under the wage protection programme pay the wages they report for their registered employees.

F-R2.quote: PDPL Article 15(3): disclosure requested by a public entity to implement another law, namely the Labour Law.

F-R3.quote: Enforcing correct payment of wages to private-sector employees, a function given to the Ministry by the Labour Law.

F-R4.quote: Employee name, national ID number, employer establishment number, registered monthly wage.

F-R5.quote: Kept for three years after the related inspection is closed, then destroyed.

F-R6.quote: Requested by the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development from the General Organization for Social Insurance.

F-R1.quote: The data will be used only to check that inspected employers pay the wages they report for their registered employees.

F-R6.quote: Requested by the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development from the General Organization for Social Insurance.

F-P1.quote: General Organization for Social Insurance, Data Management Office, privacy@gosi.example

F-P2.quote: Registering private-sector employees and their wages to calculate and collect social insurance contributions and pay benefits, and verifying with labour authorities that registered wages match the wages paid.

F-P3.quote: Processing required to implement the Social Insurance Law.

F-P4.quote: Employee name, national ID number, date of birth, employer establishment number, registered monthly wage, contribution history.

F-P5.quote: Private-sector employees registered for social insurance, and employers' authorised representatives.

F-P6.quote: The Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development, for labour law enforcement; other government entities where a law requires disclosure.

F-P7.quote: No transfer or disclosure outside the Kingdom.

F-P8.quote: Contribution records are kept for the employee's insured life and ten years after the final benefit is paid.
